sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a rabbit character. Draw this exact rabbit as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the brown sitting body with its cream tummy, without head, front paws, hind legs or tail; its top, normally under the head, rounded.
2. the head: the rabbit's head with its cheeks and pink nose, facing left as in image 1, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no mouth — keep the nose and the rosy cheek; without ears; its bottom edge rounded.
3. one ear: a long upright ear with its pink inside, with a rounded base.
4. one front paw: a small front leg with its paw, bent, with a rounded shoulder.
5. one hind leg: the big sitting hind leg with its long foot, with a rounded hip.
6. the tail: the round white cotton tail.
7. a little clover leaf with three round leaves on a short stalk.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a rabbit character; image 2 shows the same rabbit cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the rabbit's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the rabbit in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the rabbit's left eye (on the right of image 1) as it is in image 1: a dark round eye with a white sparkle.
2. the same eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
3. the same eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few lashes.
4. the same eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
5. the same eye sad: looking down, its upper lid tilted up towards the middle.
6. the mouth as it is in image 1: a small open happy smile.
7. the mouth nibbling, two little front teeth showing.
8. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, the inside pink.
9. the mouth open in a small round 'o'.
10. the mouth in a small sad frown.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a rabbit character; image 2 shows its face pieces as separate stickers. Draw four more face pieces for this rabbit, for a gentle, sweet cry, as separate stickers on one sheet: exactly the same drawing style, line, colours and size as the eyes and mouths in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in one tidy row with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the eye sad: the same dark round eye with its white sparkle as the first eye in image 2, the pupil looking straight down (centred at the bottom of the eye, not to either side), its upper lid drooping over the top of the eye and tilted, higher on the left end than the right, and a thin shine of a welling tear along the bottom rim.
2. the eye crying: gently squeezed shut, a soft downward-curving line (like a sad closed eye, not a smile), a few small lashes, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its right end.
3. the eye crying, the same as 2 but without the teardrop.
4. the mouth sobbing: the same muzzle as the mouths in image 2 (pale cheek pads with the small pink-brown nose on top), its mouth a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside, trembling.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a rabbit; image 2 shows the same rabbit cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw one single piece, centred on the sheet: the rabbit's head together with its neck, as one piece. It is exactly the head of image 2 — the same fluffy brown head with its cream muzzle and cheeks, the same small pink-brown nose and rosy cheeks, the same completely blank face (no eyes, no mouth), without ears, turned the same way (facing left), the same drawing style, colours, fur texture and line — but there is no chin line under it: the cream furry throat and the brown fur at the sides of the neck carry straight on down below the head, as wide as the head, for about half the head's height, the way the head flows into the chest in image 1, and end in a smooth rounded bottom edge. At the size the head has in image 1. Nothing else on the sheet. No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

one long ear flops down to the side, the rabbit peeks at it in surprise, then perks it back up and laughs.
